post.description:
Append a message to a group's persisted message log.

Atomic w.r.t. file IO via _save_group's tempfile-replace pattern. Not
safe under concurrent writes to the SAME group from multiple processes;
that's acceptable for the current single-uvicorn-process deployment.

Side effect — Stream C chat→agent bridge: when the incoming message is
from a user (``sender_kind == 'user'``) and the group has agent members,
we schedule an async dispatch via ``BackgroundTasks`` that calls the
configured BYOK LLM and appends agent replies back into this group's
message log. The dispatch failures are isolated — they cannot affect
the persistence success of this endpoint.

2026-05-29 — Forward the frontend BYOK credentials (``X-LLM-*`` headers,
same as ``/api/chat/completions``) into the background dispatch so the
group agent can reply using the key configured in the browser, not only a
server-side env var. ``dispatch_agent_reply`` falls back to env keys when
these are absent.

2026-05-29 (Node 接管) — ``X-SF-No-Dispatch`` header suppresses the Python
reply bridge. The Node gateway (``server/src/routes/groups-chat.ts``) now
intercepts this endpoint, persists the user message here with this header
set (so Python does NOT also reply — would double up), then generates the
agent reply via its own dispatcher (CLI/API) and POSTs it back here as a
``sender_kind='agent'`` message. Direct (non-Node) callers omit the header
and keep the legacy Python bridge as a fallback.

SSE publish — agent/system messages are pushed onto the group's event bus
so the browser sees them in real time regardless of which process wrote
them (Python bridge OR Node gateway). User messages are NOT published (the
sender already shows them optimistically; publishing would echo-duplicate).

get.description:
SSE stream of a group's live events.

Events emitted (``id:`` seq → ``event:`` line → ``data:`` JSON):
  agent.message  — an agent reply was appended to the group
  system.notice  — a bridge/system notice was appended
  agent.typing   — an agent is composing a reply (optional UX hint)

Keepalive comments every 15s keep the connection open through proxies.

2026-11-07 — Disconnect replay: frames carry a per-group monotonic ``id``.
On connect the stream first replays buffered events missing since the
client's cursor (``Last-Event-ID`` header — sent automatically by the
browser's EventSource auto-reconnect — or ``?last_event_id=`` / ``?after=``),
then continues live. Without a cursor the whole buffer is replayed; the
client dedupes by message_id so duplicates are harmless.

post.description:
RAG query over a pack's index.

层级检索优先（借鉴 StaffDeck）：hier_index 先在文档树上定位候选
文档/章节节点，再在其子树内取 chunk 合成 hits —— 命中时直接返回，每条带
`path`（doc > chapter 层级来源），响应带 `trace`（定位路径，供检索调试）。

层级索引无命中 / 构建失败 → 回落现有平铺检索：LightRAG enabled → prefer
lightrag_adapter.query_hits() and pass through the real retrieved fragments
as multiple `{text, source, score}` hits.  When the adapter can't do
structured retrieval (raises), fall back to the original behaviour: wrap the
synthesized answer as a single hit.  Disabled / not configured / query
failure → empty `hits` (never 500): callers degrade to "no citations"
instead of breaking the chat flow.

两条路径的响应都带 `graph_context`（PackGraph 图遍历扩展：query 提及的
实体 + 1 跳邻居，无 LLM、确定性）；图不存在或无命中时为 null。

get.description:
Verifier verdicts for a loop — per-iteration {iteration, score, rationale, claims[]}.

Source: the persisted loop_record iterations (step.output.loop_record).
evidence.sensor carries the LLM-as-a-Verifier fields written by
RuntimeService._sense_with_verifier (verifier_score / verifier_reasoning),
evidence.claims carries the Chain-of-Evidence claims. Non-verifier sensors

get.description:
SSE stream of loop progress for a run — replaces 5s polling.

First frame: `loop.snapshot` with the current loops state (same shape as
GET /runs/{id}/loops `data`). Subsequent frames: incremental loop-domain
facts (`loop.iteration` / `loop.completed` / `loop.halt_requested` /
`task.ledger`, plus `node.retried` carrying a loop_id) — fanned out from
RuntimeService._emit_run_event onto the RunEventBus. Supports the
Last-Event-ID header / ?last_event_id= query param for reconnection,
same as /workflow/runs/{id}/events. The stream may be attached before the
run starts (snapshot is empty then) and terminates when the run closes.

post.description:

ValidationHookSpec.title: ValidationHookSpec
ValidationHookSpec.description:
One validation hook entry inside `team.validation_hooks: [...]`.

Exactly ONE of `shell` / `webhook` / `builtin` MUST be set, matching
the `kind` discriminator. The validator below enforces this contract
so a malformed YAML (`kind=shell` with no `shell:` block, or
`kind=builtin` with both `builtin:` and `webhook:` set) gets rejected
at load time rather than at runtime.

Field invariants:

* `id` is unique within a team (the API endpoint enforces uniqueness;
  this model does not, so a partial unit-test caller can build single
  specs without round-tripping through the team record).
* `on_fail="retry"` only makes sense if `max_retries > 0`; otherwise it
  is functionally identical to `blocker` (PM decision Q12.2 — retry
  budget is independent of per-node retry).
* `expose_error_details=True` opts into shipping upstream-node
  `error.message` + `error.stack` into the hook template payload;
  default `False` redacts them per PM decision Q12.3.

ValidationHooksConfig.title: ValidationHooksConfig
ValidationHooksConfig.description:
Wrapper used by `PUT /api/teams/{id}/validation-hooks` request body.

Stored on the team record as `record["validation_hooks"] = [...]` (a
raw list — the wrapper is only for transport / validation symmetry
with `TeamWorkflow` and `TeamPolicyRequest`).

WebhookHookConfig.title: WebhookHookConfig
WebhookHookConfig.description:
POST/GET an HTTP endpoint; treat response per `success_when`.

`headers` / `body_template` may interpolate `${workspace}`, `${team_id}`,
`${results_json}`, and `${credential.<name>}` placeholders (resolved by
the runner against the Python `/api/settings` Fernet store; see H5 in
the design doc).

WebhookSuccessWhen.title: WebhookSuccessWhen
WebhookSuccessWhen.description:
Success criterion for a webhook hook.

`status_code` is always checked. If both `json_path` and `equals` are
provided, the JSON body must additionally match. `json_path` is a
minimal `$.foo.bar` style path (no expression language — kept tiny on
purpose; expr-eval is for DAG edge conditions).
